'''Kubotsu Ōji''' ('''窪津王子''') is the first of the {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|qid=Q3200355}}'s {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|熊野九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3200280}} shrines. It was located near the {{ill|Hachikenya Boat Dock|ja|八軒家船着場|qid=Q11391758}} in the {{ill|Tenma Bridge|ja|天満橋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmabashi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q18215296}} area of {{ill|Chūō-ku, Osaka|en|Chūō-ku, Osaka|qid=Q876485|lt=Chūō-ku, Osaka}}, Today, the site is marked by the {{ill|Ikasuri Shrine|en|Ikasuri Shrine|qid=Q11425667|lt=Ikasuri Shrine}} {{nihongo|Temporary Shrine|行宮}}.

Later, Kubotsu Ōji was enshrined as {{ill|Kumano shrine|en|Kumano shrine|qid=Q3200355|lt=Kumano Shrine}} near the western gate of {{ill|Shitennō-ji|en|Shitennō-ji|qid=Q339859|lt=Shitennō-ji}}. On February 10, {{ill|1915|en|1915|qid=Q2084|lt=1915}} (Taishō 4), it was relocated to {{ill|Horikoshi Shrine|ja|堀越神社|qid=Q11427801}} in {{ill|Q18989850|ja|堀越町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horikoshi Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q18989850}}, {{ill|Tennōji-ku, Osaka|en|Tennōji-ku, Osaka|qid=Q490592|lt=Tennoji-ku, Osaka}}, where it is now a subordinate shrine known as "Kumano Daiichi Ōji Shrine" (熊野第一王子社).

The {{ill|Ikasuri Shrine|en|Ikasuri Shrine|qid=Q11425667|lt=Ikasuri Shrine}} originally stood at this location but was moved to {{ill|Kyūtarō-machi|ja|久太郎町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyūtarō-machi, Osaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q60996434}} in Chūō-ku during the construction of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Castle|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大坂城|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q321242}}. Many retired emperors (*jōkō*) who undertook the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage|ja|熊野御幸|qid=DELETED_QID}} also visited this site.
